title: Kestrel Incident Runbook
format: questions: the 8 valid questions of the sample game. wrong: 2 deliberately wrong drafts; each one replaces questions[replaces] in a first draft, is refused with expected_code, then the agent resends the valid question (the refused then corrected demo step).

questions.prompt: Within how many minutes must the primary on-call engineer acknowledge a page?
questions.source_quote: The primary must acknowledge a page within 5 minutes.
questions.explanation: After 5 minutes without acknowledgement the page escalates to the secondary engineer.

questions.prompt: How long are audit logs kept?
questions.source_quote: Audit logs are kept for 400 days.
questions.explanation: Application logs are kept 30 days, but audit logs 400 days.

questions.prompt: Who must approve a rollback that touches more than one service?
questions.source_quote: A rollback that touches more than one service needs the commander's explicit approval in the channel.
questions.explanation: A single-service rollback needs no approval; more than one service needs the incident commander.

questions.prompt: Above which PostgreSQL replication lag does the on-call engineer get paged?
questions.explanation: Replication lag above 120 seconds pages as a SEV2. The 5 second figure is the failover condition.

questions.prompt: How often must the status page be updated during a SEV1?
questions.source_quote: Status page updates are due every 30 minutes during a SEV1 and every 60 minutes during a SEV2, even when there is nothing new to report.
questions.explanation: Every 30 minutes for a SEV1, even with nothing new; every 60 minutes for a SEV2.

questions.prompt: Why is the Eastport replica only a last-resort failover target?
choices: It runs an older PostgreSQL version
It can lose up to 60 seconds of writes
It is shared with the billing system
questions.source_quote: Fail over to the Eastport replica only as a last resort, because it can lose up to 60 seconds of writes.
questions.explanation: The Eastport replica is asynchronous, so a cross-region failover can lose recent writes.

questions.prompt: For how long are database backups kept?
questions.source_quote: Backups are encrypted with AES-256 and kept for 35 days.
questions.explanation: Backups are kept 35 days. 30 days is the retention of application logs, a common mix-up.

questions.prompt: Within how many business days is the written post-incident review due?
questions.source_quote: The written review is due within 5 business days, and the review meeting is held within 10 business days.
questions.explanation: The written review takes at most 5 business days; the meeting follows within 10.

question.prompt: For how long are database backups kept?
question.source_quote: Backups are encrypted with AES-256 and kept for 90 days.

question.prompt: Within how many business days is the written post-incident review due?
question.source_quote: Post-incident reviews must be written up and shared with leadership within one working week.
question.explanation: The written review takes at most 5 business days.
